rationale: G2's sole round-3 required change is addressed: R6.4 now emits all currently failing signals, and AC-17 covers mixed coverage, fresh replacement, a narrower refusal, and coverage lost through digest growth. The new reattest read-back has one accidental authority-reuse gap: its two-condition predicate does not bind the audit to the current landed SHA pair. A scratch-only real-git probe exercised the existing ReattestLandedMerge, executor ensureLandedBinding, and bead metadata helpers: reattest audited M1; a subsequent executor binding changed the pair to M2 while preserving every M1 audit key. After the #239 topology, the literal proposed read-back accepts M2 despite no reattest of M2 and despite two candidates that a fresh fallback reattest must refuse. This is an ordinary writer-composition footgun, distinct from the explicitly accepted deliberate metadata forgery. Eight existing lifecycle trust tests also passed. This reviews the specification at a593792a, not a future fallback implementation. All probe mutations stayed in the scratch clone and scratch temporary repositories; the source repository was read-only.
concrete_changes_required: Bind R4.2's reattest read-back authority to the exact identity that reattest accepted, not merely to the presence of mindspec_landed_reattest_* keys and a matching scanned branch. Define a machine-checkable attested tuple containing at least the scanned spec branch, accepted merge SHA, and accepted second parent; require equality with the independently generated candidate and current binding before automatic fallback identification. A stale, incomplete, or mismatching audit must grant no fallback authority. This can be implemented entirely in the new audit writer/reader contract without changing the executor or adding authentication. Extend AC-11 and AC-18 with an actual reattest of M1 followed by an executor binding update to M2 that preserves M1's audit, then the #239 topology: automatic read-back must refuse M2; with two owned fallback candidates, a fresh reattest must refuse Ambiguous and write nothing. Preserve the valid same-tuple reattest/read-back happy path and the no-op audit write case.

findings.title: Round-3 ask status
findings.detail: G2r3.1 — ADDRESSED. spec.md:515–523 changes the release/re-claim recovery to --allow-not-ready=<all currently failing ids>, explicitly separates uncovered diagnostics from claim authority, and retains replacement rather than union. AC-17 (:791–800) exercises one covered plus one uncovered signal, release followed by a fresh full-set re-claim, refusal of the narrower request, the MF-3/MF-4 pair, and digest-list growth while another signal stays covered. The examples generalize the exact MF-3-covered/MF-2-uncovered ordering requested previously. No prior G2 required change is PARTIAL or MISSED. The audit-identity issue below is NEW_ISSUE introduced by this round's read-back contract.

findings.title: An older reattest audit can authorize a different fallback binding without a new reattest
findings.detail: spec.md:374–378 makes automatic fallback identification an iff of the current binding naming the candidate pair and the presence of a reattest audit whose scanned branch matches. The existing audit schema has actor, time, operation, corroboration, prior pair and scanned branch (internal/lifecycle/reattest.go:356–365); its accepted pair is held in the mutable current binding, with the old pair also mentioned in free-form corroboration text. The executor's ensureLandedBinding (:1771–1774) updates only the current pair and landed_at through bead.MergeMetadata; MergeMetadata (:336–342) retains unrelated keys. Therefore a genuine audit of M1 survives a normal subsequent executor binding to M2. The scratch probe TestG2Round4StaleReattestAudit calls the real reattest engine and real executor helper, with real git and a file-backed fake bd; it confirms every audit key remains byte-equivalent, while the binding changes. Both landings are then reachable only off first-parent. The new read-back's stated conditions accept M2, although M2 was never reattested and a fresh fallback reattest must refuse the two-candidate history under R4.2(i). Evidence: stale-audit-probe.json and repo/internal/executor/g2_round4_audit_probe_test.go in this scratch directory. The future read-back is modeled literally, not claimed to have executed in production. Require an attested-identity equality check and pin this existing-writer composition in AC-11; no malicious audit write or cryptographic protection is involved.

findings.title: Deliberate audit forgery remains possible within the stated threat boundary
findings.detail: Yes: a bd writer can forge the binding and every reattest audit field, including operation, actor, timestamp and scanned branch. Those fields neither authenticate an operator nor prove the reattest command ran. R4.2 now says this explicitly, and ADR-0037 §8 forbids treating repo-file authentication as a solution at this layer. The evidence-file digest likewise binds bytes, not the truth of a justification or human approval. A repository writer can fabricate a panel registration, and a history writer can spoof merge subjects. I request no signing, trusted external store, or human-authentication mechanism. The required change above only prevents genuine stale audit data from accidentally applying to a different pair; deliberate forgery of the complete new tuple remains the documented residual.

findings.title: N4 and mapped membership retain the selection boundary
findings.detail: R1.1 now independently checks plan-form ID, unchanged FindEpicForBead lineage, and a plan mapping; removing the parent-E shortcut prevents a conflicting epic dependency from selecting a bead for the wrong spec. metadata.spec_id alone still cannot confer selection membership. N4 is informational but never default-selected; its positional exception still goes through GateReadiness and requires a fresh explicit MF-1 override rather than inheriting a marker. A no-lineage N4 cannot use that override to bypass lineage resolution: EvaluateReadiness currently errors before it produces signals, and R1.8 retains the lineage/spec guard. The existing extractBeadSectionRaw maps by ordinal heading position, while work_chunks uses explicit IDs; R1.1 must reuse those existing mappings as stated. Neither an informational empty-set exit nor either mapping by itself grants a claim or dispatch. No additional selection fail-open was established.

findings.title: Existing trust checks exercised
findings.detail: Eight existing lifecycle tests passed at the reviewed commit: forged binding with no real merge; binding at another bead's merge; anonymous-subject binding refusal; forged binding at a real anonymous merge; inconsistent binding pair (both subcases); surviving-tip contradiction; audited contradictory-binding repair; and stale older remerge binding repair. The new scratch executor probe also passed and produced stale-audit-probe.json. These verify current primitives and the demonstrated metadata persistence, not the not-yet-implemented fallback, N4 classifier, marker schema v2 or future AC suite. The original worktree remains at a593792a5795a19639deba83bff6970566d91032; no edits, lifecycle mutations or tracker mutations were made there.

findings.title: Errors in this BRIEF
findings.detail: The current O3 lens still describes selection as epic descendants union metadata.spec_id, although R1.1 now requires plan-form ID, unchanged lineage and MF-1 mapping; metadata is only a near-miss linkage for selection. The current F1 lens still calls the successor 129b, superseded by the explicit Round-4 plain-number ruling. The generic conduct example git worktree add would write worktree administrative metadata into the source repository despite the read-only rule; I used the user-authorized no-hardlinks scratch clone instead. The header's artifact destination is explicitly overridden later and by the user, so I followed verdict.json in scratch. The stale commit reference and hard-coded AC count reported in my round-3 administrative finding have been corrected in this BRIEF. These are brief discrepancies, not additional required spec changes.
